_comment: SHA-256 of the official release tarball at https://github.com/pyodide/pyodide/releases.
Recorded on first fetch over TLS from that origin, and thereafter enforced: the digest pins
the artifact against a mirror, a re-cut release or a truncated download. It is trust-on-first-
use provenance, not an independent attestation - Pyodide does not publish a signed checksum
file - and it is recorded here so that every later run is verified rather than trusting.
To add a version: run `prepare-runtime --version X --print-digest` and paste the result.
`core` is the SHA-256 of each essential asset AS EXTRACTED FROM THE VERIFIED RELEASE
ARCHIVE above. It is the anchor a warm cache is checked against: a stamp written into a
cache directory is written by the same process that wrote the files beside it, so it
cannot vouch for them. These values can, because they come from an artifact whose own
digest is pinned. A --sha256 passed on the command line for an unrecorded version has no
such anchor and stays trust-on-first-use; the verifier says which case it is in.
